stem: Which statement is NOT part of the modern cell theory?
option_a: All living things are made of one or more cells.
option_b: The cell is the basic unit of structure and function in living things.
option_c: All cells come from pre-existing cells.
option_d: Cells can form on their own from nonliving matter.
explanation: Spontaneous generation was disproven; cells only come from other cells.

stem: According to the cell theory, what is the smallest unit that can carry out all the processes of life?
explanation: The cell is the basic unit of structure and function; atoms and molecules are not alive.

stem: A student looks at pond water, a thin slice of onion skin, and cells scraped from her own cheek. She finds cells in every living sample. Which part of the cell theory do her observations support?
option_a: All cells come from pre-existing cells.
option_b: All living things are made of one or more cells.
option_c: Cells contain DNA that is passed on during cell division.
option_d: Cells can form from nonliving matter.
explanation: Cells found in many different organisms supports that all living things are made of cells.

stem: The modern cell theory added ideas to the original three statements. Which of the following is one of those additions?
option_a: Cells contain hereditary information (DNA) that is passed from cell to cell during cell division.
option_b: Only plants and animals are made of cells.
option_c: All cells are the same size and shape.
option_d: Cells do not need energy to carry out their functions.
explanation: Modern additions include DNA passed on during division, energy flow, and similar chemistry in all cells.

stem: Louis Pasteur boiled broth in a flask to kill all microorganisms and kept it sealed. No new microorganisms grew in the broth. Which part of the cell theory does this experiment support?
option_a: All living things are made of cells.
option_b: Cells are the basic unit of life.
option_c: All cells come from pre-existing cells.
explanation: No existing cells in the flask → no new cells formed. New cells only come from cells that already exist.

stem: Which structure is found in BOTH prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
explanation: All cells have ribosomes, a cell membrane, cytoplasm, and DNA.

stem: What is the main feature that separates eukaryotic cells from prokaryotic cells?
option_a: Eukaryotic cells have DNA; prokaryotic cells do not.
option_b: Eukaryotic cells have a nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles; prokaryotic cells do not.
option_c: Eukaryotic cells have a cell membrane; prokaryotic cells do not.
option_d: Eukaryotic cells are always single-celled; prokaryotic cells are always multicellular.
explanation: A membrane-bound nucleus and organelles is the defining difference.

stem: A scientist observes an unknown cell with a cell wall, ribosomes, and circular DNA floating in a nucleoid region. It has no nucleus and no mitochondria. This cell is most likely a…
explanation: Nucleoid, no nucleus, no mitochondria = prokaryote.

stem: A student claims that a newly discovered single-celled organism must be prokaryotic because it is made of only one cell. Which observation would provide the BEST evidence that the student's claim is wrong?
option_b: The organism has a cell membrane surrounding its cytoplasm.
option_c: The organism's DNA is enclosed inside a membrane-bound nucleus.
option_d: The organism is too small to see without a microscope.
explanation: Many eukaryotes are unicellular; a membrane-bound nucleus proves it is eukaryotic.

stem: Which group of organisms is made of eukaryotic cells?
explanation: Bacteria and archaea are prokaryotes; viruses are not cells.

stem: Which number labels the structure that contains the cell's DNA and controls the cell's activities?
stimulus_text: Use the cell model below to answer questions 11–13 (labels 1–5).
explanation: Label 1 = nucleus. (2 cell membrane, 3 ribosome, 4 mitochondrion, 5 rough ER)

stem: Structure #5 is a folded membrane system covered with ribosomes. What is structure #5?
explanation: Ribosomes on its surface make it rough ER; smooth ER has none.

stem: This model shows an animal cell. Which structures would a student need to add to turn it into a model of a plant cell?
explanation: Plant cells add a cell wall and chloroplasts (and a large central vacuole).

stem: A student builds an analogy model comparing a cell to a school. Which pairing is the BEST match?
option_a: Cell membrane = the front office, because it makes all the decisions
option_b: Nucleus = the hallways, because things travel through them
option_c: Cell membrane = the doors and security, because it controls what enters and leaves
option_d: Mitochondria = the lockers, because they store things
explanation: The membrane is selectively permeable, like doors and security.

stem: A student draws a model with a nucleus, mitochondria, chloroplasts, a cell wall, and ribosomes, then labels it “Bacterial Cell.” What is the main error in this model?
option_b: Bacteria do not have a cell wall.
option_c: Bacteria do not have a nucleus or membrane-bound organelles like mitochondria and chloroplasts.
option_d: Nothing is wrong; this is a correct model of a bacterial cell.
explanation: Prokaryotes lack a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.
